# K-210 Plant Air Compressor: Control Narrative
## Section: Start, Stop and Protection

Values marked **[TBC]** were not in the source data. They are proposed and must be confirmed against the vendor documents before the narrative is issued.

### 1. Scope and equipment

K-210 is a 900 kW, three-stage integrally geared centrifugal air compressor with a 6.6 kV motor and soft starter. It is started and stopped by the operator from the DCS.

| Tag | Function |
|---|---|
| ZC-210 / ZT-210 | Inlet guide vane (IGV) command / position |
| FV-211 | Blow-off valve to atmosphere (fails open **[TBC]**) |
| P-212 | AC auxiliary oil pump (main pump is shaft-driven) |
| PT-213 | Oil header pressure (normal 2.5 bar) |
| TT-214 | Oil temperature |
| VT-215/216/217 | Vibration, stages 1/2/3 |

The discharge header pressure controller holds 7.0 barg. Its tag is not given **[TBC]**.

### 2. Operating states

| State | Description |
|---|---|
| STOPPED | Motor off, ready or not ready depending on permissives |
| PRE-LUBE | P-212 running, permissives being proven |
| STARTING | Soft starter ramping the motor |
| UNLOADED RUN | At speed, IGVs at minimum, FV-211 open |
| LOADED RUN | Pressure control active |
| STOPPING | Unload, stop, and post-lube |
| TRIPPED | Latched until reset |

### 3. Start permissives (all required, "Ready to Start")

1. No active trip, and the trip latch is reset.
2. Oil temperature TT-214 is above 25 °C. Below this, the tank heater is enabled and the start is blocked. The heater is switched off at a higher setpoint **[TBC]**.
3. P-212 is running and PT-213 is at or above 2.0 bar **[TBC]**. This proves lubrication before rotation.
4. ZT-210 confirms IGVs at the closed or start position.
5. FV-211 is confirmed fully open.
6. VT-215/216/217 signals are healthy, with no active trip level.
7. The soft starter is healthy and the 6.6 kV breaker is available. The motor protection relay is not tripped.
8. Motor start limits are satisfied (see 4).
9. The emergency stop is not active.

The DCS shows each permissive individually so the operator can see what is blocking a start.

### 4. Motor start limits

- No more than 3 starts in any rolling 60 minutes.
- At least 20 minutes between hot starts. Unless the vendor defines a cold-start criterion **[TBC]**, apply the 20-minute interval after every start attempt.
- Failed or aborted starts count as starts.
- The DCS displays the starts counter and the time remaining until the next start is allowed.
- Trip resets do not clear the counter or timers. They cannot be overridden from the DCS.

### 5. Start sequence

1. The operator selects START. If TT-214 is below 25 °C, the heater runs and the request is held or rejected.
2. The DCS starts P-212 (if not already running), drives IGVs to the start position and opens FV-211.
3. When all permissives are met, the DCS closes the 6.6 kV breaker and starts the soft starter.
4. Start supervision:
   - Motor run feedback must be confirmed within the vendor acceleration time **[TBC]**. Otherwise the start is aborted and counted.
   - PT-213 low-low and the vibration trip remain active during starting. The vibration trip delay may be extended during acceleration, per the vendor **[TBC]**.
5. At full speed and after a stable run time **[TBC]**, the state is UNLOADED RUN.
6. P-212 stays running until PT-213 is at or above 2.3 bar **[TBC]** on the shaft-driven pump alone for a set time **[TBC]**. It then stops and goes to standby (auto-start armed).
7. The operator selects LOAD, or loading is automatic after warm-up **[TBC]**. The pressure controller then releases the IGVs and FV-211 closes as the compressor takes load.

### 6. Capacity control while running

- The pressure controller holds the header at 7.0 barg by positioning the IGVs through ZC-210.
- If demand falls below the IGV minimum flow, FV-211 opens to vent the excess and keep the machine out of surge. Long periods of venting are signalled to the operator as an efficiency alarm.
- The vendor surge line has priority over the pressure controller. See 8.

### 7. Normal stop

1. The operator selects STOP.
2. IGVs go to minimum and FV-211 opens. Unloaded status is confirmed by ZT-210 and the FV-211 position, with a time limit **[TBC]**.
3. The DCS commands the soft starter and breaker to stop. The motor coasts down.
4. P-212 starts with the stop command and runs through coastdown (post-lube). It stops only after zero speed is confirmed plus a hold time **[TBC]**.
5. The restart timers in 4 begin counting.

### 8. Surge protection

- The vendor controller calculates the surge line. When the operating point reaches it, FV-211 opens to restore flow. The valve is reclosed in a controlled way once the point is back inside a margin.
- A surge event counter runs. If the number of surge events exceeds the vendor limit within the vendor period **[TBC]**, the machine trips (see 9).
- On any stop or trip, FV-211 opens immediately so the machine is not left to surge during coastdown.

### 9. Protection

| Condition | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Oil header pressure low | 1.8 bar | Alarm. P-212 auto-starts at 2.0 bar **[TBC]**, above the alarm. |
| Oil header pressure low-low | 1.3 bar | **Trip.** Short delay **[TBC]**, bypassed only for the vendor-defined start window with P-212 proven. |
| Oil temperature low | Below 25 °C | Start blocked. Heater on. |
| Oil temperature high | **[TBC]** | Alarm and trip per vendor. |
| Vibration, any stage | 40 µm | Alarm |
| Vibration, any stage | 60 µm | **Trip.** Short delay **[TBC]**. |
| Vibration transmitter fault | Bad signal | Alarm. Fault handling is a design decision: see below. |
| Surge, excessive | Vendor limit | **Trip** |
| P-212 fails to start on demand | | Alarm. If PT-213 continues to fall, the 1.3 bar trip applies. |
| Motor faults, soft starter fault, overcurrent, motor winding or bearing temperatures | Per motor protection relay | **Trip** |
| Emergency stop | Hardwired | **Trip**, independent of the DCS |

**Vibration trip logic (design decision).** There is only one probe per stage, so a 2oo3 vote could miss a real single-stage problem. This narrative proposes a trip on any one probe above 60 µm, with a short delay. A faulty probe raises an alarm and is excluded from the trip logic after a time, so a single failure cannot cause a spurious shutdown. Confirm with the vendor and the project's SIL or reliability requirements.

### 10. Trip response

On any trip:
1. The motor breaker is opened (soft starter is bypassed or stopped).
2. FV-211 opens and the IGVs go to minimum or closed.
3. P-212 auto-starts for post-lube, unless the trip is caused by an oil system fault where continued operation is unsafe **[TBC]**.
4. The first-out cause is captured and displayed.
5. The trip latches. The operator must acknowledge, confirm the cause is cleared, and reset. Restart is subject to the limits in 4.

### 11. Open items for confirmation

1. FV-211 failure position and the action on loss of air or signal.
2. Header pressure transmitter and controller tags.
3. High oil temperature alarm and trip values, heater on and off setpoints.
4. Auto-start and stop pressures for P-212, post-lube time, and the PT-213 trip delay.
5. Vendor definition of a hot start, and the acceleration time.
6. Vibration trip delay during acceleration, and the voting decision above.
7. Surge-count trip limit and the vendor reclose logic.
8. Whether loading after warm-up is automatic or operator initiated.
